text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed after a day of heavy trading in Medellin fueled by a U.S. investor's multi-million dollar investment in supermarket chain Cadenalco, brokers said.

They said an anonymous buyer from the United States had snapped up eight million ordinary shares of Gran Cadena de Almacenes de Colombia (Cadenalco) in a deal valued at $6.8 million that was quietly handled through the Medellin stock exchange, giving someone 3.99 percent of the company's already issued ordinary shares.
A source at Cadenalco said both the buyer and seller were entitled to anonymity under secrecy provisions laid down by Colombia's securities commission.

Cadenalo closed unchanged at 900 pesos per share despite the transaction and Medellin's IBOMED general price index edged up just 0.15 percent at 13,433.54 pesos per share. Total volume in Medellin was well above average at 8.4 billion pesos.
Bogota's IBB index ended down 0.55 percent, meanwhile, closing at 861.25 on a lackluster volume of 904.1 million pesos.
Other winners included cement maker Cementos Argos, which rose 1.73 percent to close at 5,290 pesos a share, and Cementos Diamante, which closed up 1.31 percent at 3,850 per share.
Losers were led by brewer Bavaira, which fell 3.06 percent to 3,800 pesos per share and Banco Industrial Colombiano, which dropped 1.42 percent to end at 3,450 pesos per share.
"The dips were clearly due to profit taking," one Bogota- based broker said. He added that they were relatively insignificant, however, because of low trading volumes.
